components.basis: Transfinite Lindenbaum lemma stated for an arbitrary ordinal-indexed enumeration (154-165). The proof defines the sequence by transfinite recursion with zero, successor (consistency case split) and limit (union) clauses (167-180); proves the chain claim by transfinite induction (182-186); proves consistency at successor and limit stages with the finite-support/maximum argument including empty support (188-200); and proves maximality via rejection at stage alpha+1 and monotonicity of derivability (202-209).

The Henkin--Lindenbaum lemma builds the witness-saturated Sigma^H by transfinite recursion (240-255), then at 257-265 fixes a bijective enumeration of Fm(L^H) and applies lem:transfinite-lindenbaum; the witness property follows at 265-268. No appeal to the propositional omega-Lindenbaum lemma (lem:prop-lindenbaum) occurs in the chapter; the only reference to lem:prop-mcs (19-32) transfers MCS closure clauses with a written first-order deductive-closure proof.

The maximality construction displays the successor case (172-176, 190), the limit case (178-179, 190-200) and the chain argument (182-186, used at 198-199 and 203). It is consumed at 263-265 with no out-of-scope appeal to the propositional lemma. The parallel treatment handbook/annex/p02/first-order-completeness.tex is not \input by handbook/annex/p02.tex and was not credited.
